messages:
ada: Hey team, first-day snag: redwoodctl profile switching + local-test plugin race causing my sample app to start with stale creds and 502s. Thought i'd share repro and ask for best short-term fixes.

ada: Steps: macOS Ventura, redwoodctl v0.31.2, I have two profiles (personal, team). Workflow: `redwoodctl auth login --profile team --service-account-key $SA && redwoodctl local-test --profile team --mount ./examples:/app/examples --plugins sample-proxy` ran into trouble when I switched profiles quickly.

pete: What happened exactly? paste minimal logs.

ada: logs: 
```
INFO auth: login success, wrote token to cache (/Users/ada/.redwood/tokens/team.json)
INFO profiles: active profile set to team
INFO local-test: starting runtime (plugins: sample-proxy)
WARN profiles: profile-change detected, reloading (source: cli)
ERROR auth: cached token expired, attempted refresh -> 401
INFO local-test: plugin sample-proxy started with token from cache
ERROR proxy: upstream 502 Bad Gateway (401 from control plane)
WARN local-test: retrying plugin init in 300ms
```
Result: local-test kept running but the sample-proxy presented 502s because plugin used an expired token that got refreshed concurrently and wrote a new token file while the plugin still had the old credentials in memory.

mikko: Sounds like a read-write race on the token cache + plugin startup. Do you have any env like REDWOOD_SESSION_TTL or custom token-refresh hooks?

ada: no, default settings. This is reproducible if I run `redwoodctl auth login --profile team` and almost immediately `redwoodctl local-test --profile team` — sometimes the runtime picks up the pre-refresh token. Repro rate ~30%.

pete: Short-term workaround: run `sleep 0.5` between login and local-test or use `redwoodctl profiles set-active team && redwoodctl auth refresh --profile team` and wait for success before starting local-test. Also `REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(redwoodctl auth token --profile team)` and run local-test with `REDWOOD_TOKEN` in env so plugin sees consistent token.

ada: adding `--wait-for-token` flag would be awesome. Right now i hack `until redwoodctl auth whoami --profile team; do sleep 0.2; done` in my script.

mikko: We'll address in two ways: 1) make token cache writes atomic and add file lock so readers see a consistent token; 2) add a small `redwoodctl local-test --wait-auth` flag that waits for an active, refreshable token before launching plugins.

auth-bot: Filed infra#4520: token-cache atomic write + advisory file lock for readers. Filed infra#4521: add CLI `--wait-auth` flag and make plugin loader acquire read-after-refresh consistency.

pete: Also note plugins that load tokens from disk at startup should re-read the token after a short grace window if they get 401s on first request; a fallback retry with a re-read prevents transient 502s.

ada: Another thing: onboarding sample app crashed with `bind: address already in use` after a failed plugin restart, causing local-test to spin. I think local-test should fail fast if plugins repeatedly fail.

mikko: Good point. We'll add a plugin-health policy: after N failures within T seconds, local-test will fail with a clear error (and nonzero code) so CI doesn't loop forever. Also we'll add `--ephemeral-port` to pick a free host port when collisions happen.

ops-bot: Followups created: infra#4522 plugin-health policy, infra#4523 --ephemeral-port flag. Also add docs note in onboarding for `REDWOOD_TOKEN` env and the `auth whoami` wait hack.

ada: Short-term script I used that made onboarding smooth: 
```
# bootstrapping script
redwoodctl auth login --profile team --service-account-key "$SA" --output token > /tmp/rw_token
export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rw_token)
# ensure token usable
until redwoodctl auth whoami --profile team >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 0.2; done
# start local-test
redwoodctl local-test --profile team --mount "$(pwd)/examples:/app/examples" --plugins sample-proxy
```
This made the sample app start reliably.

mikko: Thanks for the repro + script. We'll prioritize atomic token writes and the --wait-auth flag. Also adding a tiny integration test that runs login+local-test in quick succession to catch regressions.

ada: great, thanks. filing a gist with minimal repro and my script: https://gist.github.com/ada/61f0b9. I'll follow up on infra threads. :thumbsup:
